sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - Marketplace FBA Store

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Panama–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT), as amended by Law 70 of 2019 and Law 127 of 2021, implementing Executive Decrees No. 201/2016 and No. 178/2016; UBO disclosure obligations additionally grounded in Law 52 of 2016 (abolition of bearer shares) and the Public Registry's unified UBO (NIC) registration rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública de Constitución) executed before a Panamanian notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (notary pricing set by law; registration thereafter with the Public Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization — no apostille required; direct registration with the Public Registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of founder's passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization by the Panamanian Consulate if the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or registry extract of corporate founder (applicable only if founder is a legal person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry / Registrar of Companies of the founding jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank professional reference / status letter confirming the founder's financial standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank or financial institution of the founder's residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered agent acceptance letter and resident agent identification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Panamanian attorney or licensed resident agent firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic issuance executed in Panama; no apostille needed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory EDD for any founder, council member, protector, or beneficiary who qualifies as a PEP under Law 23/2015 (and FATF Recommendation 12). Implement automated screening against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and the Panamanian Ministry of Economy and Finance / UAF national sanctions list. Screening frequency: initial Go/No-Go and ongoing continuous monitoring. Positive hits trigger Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero within 48 hours and immediate freeze pursuant to asset freezing orders.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Ventanilla Única / Online Name Reservation Portal (visit www.registropublico.gob.pa; attorney e-filing via the 'Sistema Integrado de Presentación' available to registered law firms)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed in Latin/Roman script (Spanish is the working language of the Public Registry). A foundation name may be in a language other than Spanish but the Registry will require a transliteration into Latin characters and a Spanish translation for indexation. The name must include the word 'Foundation' or 'Fundación' or an accepted abbreviation and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered legal entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banc, Banco, Banking, Credit, Finance, Financiera, Fiduciaria, Trust, Fiduciario
Ministry, State, Government, National Treasury, Official, Municipal
Red Cross, Nobel, Olympic (and other internationally protected designations)
S.A., Sociedad Anónima, Corp., Inc., LLC, and any corporate suffix implying a stock company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant or registered attorney must submit a written request for reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) to the same Public Registry officer within 5 business days, together with a proposed alternative or a legal memorandum rebutting similarity/prohibition. On second denial, an apelación (hierarchical appeal) may be filed with the Director General del Registro Público within 10 business days. Final judicial challenge is available via acción contencioso-administrativa before the Supreme Court (Sala Tercera) within 30 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are accepted solely in the context of a licensed agent's registered-office address maintained physically in Panama. A Private Interest Foundation is not required to establish any logistical premises for an Amazon FBA online retail model, but a direct, independent virtual office for substantive business operations (e.g., inventory storage, procurement) is not recognized for tax/economic-substance purposes. E-commerce trading may require a separate Panamanian commercial vehicle (S.A.) if the foundation itself is intended to be the active trading entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; under a standard low-risk FBA e-commerce mandate, probability of an unannounced on-site inspection at the registered agent's office is below 5% annually. Site inspections would generally occur only upon the order of the Public Registry, the Tax Authority (DGI), or the UAF/AML supervisor in the context of specific red flags or a court warrant.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation fee (single query)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff approved by the Direction General for each name request; market rate between USD 20–30.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and execution of the Private Interest Foundation Charter (Pacto Fundacional)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian notary and law firm (private practitioners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional benchmark for standard PIFs; notarial fee schedule per Escritura Pública plus attorney drafting fee of USD 400–700.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year resident agent and registered-office service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent / registered law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard Panamanian registered-agent annual fee for PIFs, ranging USD 450–650 per year.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization batch for founder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Secretary of State / Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the founder's jurisdiction and, if required, Panamanian Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille fee (average USD 15–50) plus communication/courier costs; estimated for 3–5 source documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC UBO due-diligence package, PEP and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance/KYC service provider (e.g., World-Check, LexisNexis or equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk e-commerce FBA background screening; includes UBO organigram and OFAC/UN/EU list verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry registration and inscription fee for the foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for foundation registration (approximately USD 250–350 depending on authorized patrimony and page volume).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Act), as amended by Law 32 of 2011, Articles 1–49; supplemented by the Commercial Code for auxiliary matters
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Private Interest Foundation Section (Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a nominal initial endowment (commonly USD 10,000) is required and must be transferred or allocated to the foundation's registered assets. No escrow account is mandated by Panamanian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF is duly incorporated under Law 25 of 1995 and accepts its initial endowment of USD 10,000 subscribed by the founder as contemplated in the Foundation Charter. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Foundation shall be at [address in Panama City], Panama, as designated by the Resident Agent. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed as members of the Foundation Council, with powers to administer assets, appoint and remove beneficiaries, and exercise all powers granted by the Foundation Charter and Law 25 of 1995. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Resident Agent is authorized to file all documents and effect all statutory registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Foundation Charter Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Online Services (Registro Público de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed foundation name (e.g., 'PA_PIF') through the Registry's online name reservation portal. Upon approval, instruct counsel to draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish, specifying the foundation name, purpose, initial endowment, council members, beneficiary regime, and any reserved powers.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of founder and initial council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, submit 2–3 alternative names. If charter elements are defective, amend and resubmit in accordance with Registry comments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Panamanian notary to execute the Foundation Charter. Verify the identity of the founder and council members, and obtain the notarial protocol number. Ensure the Resident Agent's assignment is recorded in the charter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistencies, rectify signatures or missing pages and execute a corrective document. Re-notarization may be required if substantive amendments are introduced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Private Interest Foundation Section (Registro Público de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter together with the official registration application and proof of payment of the registry fees. The Registrar reviews the instrument for legal compliance and assigns an inscription number (inscripción) in the Foundations Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or notes defects, file a corrective brief with supporting documents within the statutory appeal period. An urgent inscription (inscripción urgente) may be requested where expedited completion is essential.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Foundation Certificate and Qualification Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Certification Desk (Registro Público de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Certificado de Existencia (Certificate of Existence), the certified copy of the registered Charter, and the certificate of foundation council composition. Arrange apostille or legalization if the certificates will be used abroad.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificates are delayed, request a written status note. For urgent use, request priority issuance at the Certificaciones window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a duly recorded organization meeting to approve the First Board/Foundation Council Resolution, adopt the registered office, and appoint officers. If the foundation will conduct any taxable activity in Panama, apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and, if a physical establishment exists, obtain the municipal aviso de operación. Pure foreign-source Amazon FBA retail does not require a municipal operating license. Maintain statute books and minutes at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Appointment of Resident Agent and officers
RUC application (if economically active in Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or municipality issues a query, respond with sworn declarations confirming the absence of local production or warehousing. If any physical activity arises in the future, apply for the corresponding operating license under the competent authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no manufacturing or physical establishment in Panama for ISIC 4791 online marketplace retail
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – pure online marketplace retail (Amazon FBA) with no physical premises in Panama

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No EIA required for virtual/online retail operations without physical infrastructure or emissions sources
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC, or waste-handling discharge sources exist for this scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – no workplace or physical establishment requiring fire safety certification, structural load inspection, or occupational clearance. If a home office is used, general building code compliance and electrical safety are recommended but not statutorily licensed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), República de Panamá; tax administration online portal: SITIO (Sistema Integrado Tributario de Ingresos en Línea) via https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa. Customs counterpart: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá (ANA) via Sistema Integrado de Aduanas (SIA). Foundation registry counterpart: Registro Público de Panamá (RPP).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Draft and register the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with the Registro Público de Panamá under the Private Interest Foundations Law (Ley 25 de 1995), filing the Foundation Charter and Foundation Regulations, appointing a resident registered agent, and satisfying the minimum capital requirement (typically USD 10,000 or such amount specified in the charter). Step 2: Determine Panamanian tax nexus. A PIF conducting Amazon FBA cross-border e-commerce where sales, customers, and fulfillment centers are located outside Panamá derives only foreign-source income, which is outside Panamá's territorial tax base; no RUC is statutorily required in that posture. Step 3: If any Panamanian-source activity arises (Panamanian payroll, local warehouse, domestic marketplace sales, import/export from Panamá), apply for RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) through SITIO by submitting the RUC application, certified copy of the Foundation Charter, registered agent certificate, evidence of fiscal address in Panamá, and a notarized power of attorney appointing a resident legal representative. Step 4: For non-resident foreign digital platforms and suppliers, obtain a non-resident RUC through SITIO and appoint a local fiscal agent for ITBMS compliance on supplies to Panamanian consumers. Step 5: If a physical Panamanian establishment is maintained, obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación (business license) and any applicable health/fire approvals. Step 6: Register with ANA for a customs exporter code if goods will be physically exported from Panamá. Step 7: Request from DGI a taxpayer-registration certificate, tax-residence certificate, or non-residence certificate, as required for foreign reporting and banking compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (Panama-source income only). The PIF is a separate juridical person subject to entity-level Panamanian income tax solely on income derived from Panamanian sources; foreign-source online retail, Amazon FBA order fulfillment, marketplace intermediary fees, and offshore service profits are excluded from Panamanian income tax and ITBMS. The PIF is not a pass-through entity; distributions to beneficiaries are non-deductible and, when originating from foreign-source foundation income, are not taxable in Panamá.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box election comparable to U.S. Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3. Entity tax classification follows foundation and corporate statute. Available elections and mechanisms: (i) voluntary registration as an ITBMS and income-tax taxpayer to claim input tax credits and file export refunds; (ii) election to use the simplified small-taxpayer indirect-tax regime for annual gross turnover up to USD 36,000; (iii) election to classify qualifying services supplied to non-residents as exported services under DGI approval (Declaración de Servicio Exportado), applying 0% ITBMS; (iv) election to domicile the PIF or the commercial activity in a special economic zone or SEM regime (e.g., Panamá Pacífico) where statutory; and (v) adoption of foundation distribution and investment policies to maintain territorial-source treatment and mitigate hybrid-mismatch exposure abroad. Panama has no domestic CFC or hybrid-mismatch rules but participates in OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework information exchange and substance-review practices.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's consumption transfer tax functionally equivalent to VAT/GST).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: any person habitually transferring taxable goods or services in Panamá must register for ITBMS. A simplified small-taxpayer regime applies to annual gross income not exceeding USD 36,000 (B/.36,000, Panamanian Balboa pegged 1:1 to USD). Non-resident digital service suppliers and marketplace platforms are required to register as non-resident ITBMS taxpayers for supplies made to Panamanian consumers under Executive Decree 223 of 2020, with no published numeric threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory fiscal electronic invoicing applies to registered taxpayers under Law 25 of 2017 and DGI regulations, administered through SITIO. Taxpayers must issue electronic invoices and electronic tax documents in XML with a DGI authorization code and QR code, transmitted to DGI before or at the moment of issuance (near-real-time fiscal clearance). Large taxpayers transmit documents via DGI-authorized web services/API (JSON/XML/SOAP); smaller taxpayers use SITIO's online invoice tool or certified invoicing software. Non-resident ITBMS taxpayers must issue DGI-compliant electronic invoices bearing the non-resident RUC. All amounts must be expressed in USD/Balboa.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% ITBMS applies where tangible goods are permanently exported from Panamanian customs territory, evidenced by an ANA/SIA customs export declaration and physical departure of the goods. Services: 0% applies to exported services rendered to a non-resident recipient, used or exploited wholly outside Panamá, and paid with funds originating from abroad, as certified by DGI. In an Amazon FBA model where orders are fulfilled from overseas Amazon warehouses, the goods never enter Panamanian customs territory; the corresponding FBA seller profits are foreign-source and remain entirely outside Panamá's territorial tax base and ITBMS, while any Panamanian input ITBMS (e.g., local warehouse or logistics services) is recoverable only where the complete export documentation chain is maintained and the ITBMS return (Form 204) is filed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas / DUA authorized through ANA-SIA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Panamanian customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / bank credit evidence demonstrating receipt of export proceeds from abroad
DGI exported-services declaration (Declaración de Servicio Exportado) for service zero-rating
Amazon marketplace settlement report and FBA shipment evidence substantiating foreign fulfillment and foreign customer destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may audit export zero-rating claims within the standard five-year prescription period, extended to seven years where returns are omitted or supported by false documents; fraud is not subject to prescription under Panama's fiscal enforcement framework. If the export or foreign-source nature is not substantiated, DGI reclassifies the transaction as a domestic taxable transfer, retroactively assessing ITBMS at 7%, statutory default interest, a negligence surcharge of up to 50% of the omitted tax, or a fraud surcharge of up to 100% (with higher sanctions for repeat violations), and disallowing any refunded input credits. Possession or use of false customs declarations, false bills of lading, or false foreign-remittance certificates exposes the PIF and its officers to Tax Code fines, administrative suspension from ANA authorized-exporter programs, and criminal liability under Ley 70 de 2019 (fiscal criminal procedure), including imprisonment for aggravated tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank and no foreign exchange administration. The monetary system is fully dollarized: the U.S. dollar is legal tender and the Panamanian balboa exists only as a nominal unit for coinage. The Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama, established 1904) acts as the State's fiscal agent and clearing agent and operates the domestic clearinghouse, but it is not a monetary authority and issues no currency. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama, SBP) supervises banking activity under Decreto Ley 2 de 2008 and administers AML/CFT obligations. The Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) administers the beneficial ownership registry under Ley 21 de 2017. Monetary and exchange conditions are effectively determined by the U.S. Federal Reserve under Panama's complete dollarization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility exists. Panama imposes no exchange controls, no prior approval for cross-border payments, no restrictions on profit remittance, dividends, interest, capital repatriation, or distributions by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF). Because the base currency is the U.S. dollar, Amazon FBA revenues, which are predominantly USD-denominated marketplace settlements, require no jurisdiction-level conversion. The practical profit-remittance hurdles are not legal but operational: banks will require proof of lawful source of funds, updated PIF council resolutions, disclosure of beneficiaries, CRS/FATCA tax self-certification, and evidence that the PIF's foreign-source e-commerce income is outside Panama's territorial income tax scope under the Código Fiscal. A PIF with opaque reserved-beneficiary provisions will face enhanced due diligence and lower onboarding viability despite the absence of exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama applies no surrender requirement, no mandatory export-proceeds conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline. The required conversion percentage is 0%. Export proceeds, including Amazon FBA marketplace settlements, may be retained abroad in USD, converted freely, or remitted to Panama without authorization. The only compliance overlay is ordinary AML/KYC and source-of-funds documentation, together with documentary consistency between Amazon settlement reports and the bank transaction narrative.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: RAITING: MEDIUM-HIGH as a settlement and collection layer, but MEDIUM as a regulatory substitute for a Panamanian licensed banking relationship. Panama does not maintain a standalone electronic money institution (EMI) license. Offshore fintech/EMI platforms such as Airwallex, Stripe, Payoneer, and Amazon Pay can lawfully serve the PIF as payment processors, disbursement agents, and USD collection-account providers in their own jurisdictions, and can sweep funds into Panama by SWIFT MT103 or ACH-to-SWIFT bridges. However, any entity performing deposit-taking or financial intermediation in Panama requires authorization under the banking regime of Decreto Ley 2 de 2008, so a foreign EMI cannot hold a Panamanian client balance or issue a Panamanian IBAN. The SBP KYC rules require the Panamanian bank to perform equivalent customer due diligence or rely on the fintech only with adequate risk controls. For Amazon FBA, the practical flow is Amazon Seller Central settlement to a USD account or PSP account in the United States, followed by a treasury sweep into the PIF's Panama operational account; Airwallex and Stripe are viable for revenue collection, currency conversion at market rates, and supplier disbursement, provided the fund trail is transparent and the PIF remains the principal seller of record. Legal blockers include unlicensed pass-through of third-party funds, Amazon settlement reports inconsistent with declared revenues, and failure to identify reserved beneficiaries in the fintech's KYC file.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panama's SBP customer due diligence regulation (Acuerdo No. 1 de 2014, as amended) does not universally require a physical board meeting in Panama for PIF account opening, but in practice tier-1 Panamanian banks require at least one natural-person signatory, normally the PIF Council president, to attend a personal KYC interview at the bank branch. Remote onboarding using video conference is accepted only by select banks and only when the foundation structure is fully transparent, all beneficial owners are disclosed, and the KYC package is certified by a notary or a known corporate introducer. Non-face-to-face onboarding automatically triggers enhanced due diligence, which usually lengthens approval and may require higher minimum deposits. The safest blueprint is for the founder or a council member with signing authority to appear physically in Panama City with original or apostilled documentation, a PIF good-standing certificate, current council resolutions, full UBO schedule, and a legal opinion under Ley 25 de 1995. There is no statutory right to remote-only opening; onboarding viability increases materially with physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque PIF structure with reserved beneficiaries, protector powers, and undeclared ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Foundation Charter and registered statutes (Registro Público), full UBO schedule filed with the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales under Ley 21 de 2017, notarized Protector consent, Council resolution appointing signatories and approving account opening, Panamanian legal opinion confirming the PIF's existence, non-distribution constraints, and beneficial ownership under Ley 25 de 1995.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Amazon FBA revenues without matching commercial documentation, invoices, or inventory trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amazon Seller Central settlement reports covering all payout cycles, Payout reconciliation statements from Stripe, Airwallex, Payoneer, or Amazon Pay, order-level commercial invoices or tax invoices issued to the marketplace, FBA inbound and warehouse inventory receipts, supplier purchase orders and supplier invoices, customs entry summaries for goods imported into fulfillment countries, and a signed directors' resolution identifying Amazon and PSPs as settlement agents only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity pass-through pattern indicating third-party collection or undisclosed factoring of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury and fund-flow policy, flow charts showing buyer to Amazon to PSP to Panama PIF and then to suppliers, marketplace seller agreement establishing the PIF as principal and seller of record, transaction monitoring records, absence of unrelated third-party payments, and an AML compliance program proportionate to the Low_Risk_Standard classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media hits on founder, council members, or beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Time-stamped OFAC, UN, EU, and UK sanctions screening results, PEP self-certification forms, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, passport and proof of residence, negative-media search report, and an enhanced due diligence memorandum prepared by a compliance officer or external counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax ambiguity of the PIF's foreign e-commerce income causing bank de-risking or withholding confusion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Territorial tax opinion from Panamanian tax counsel under the Código Fiscal and Ley 8 de 2010 confirming that foreign-source Amazon FBA sales are outside Panamanian income tax, ITBMS analysis confirming no 7% transfer tax on sales consummated outside Panama, CRS/FATCA self-certification forms, and any relevant tax registration or exemption certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial PIF endowment under Ley 25 de 1995 must be fully constituted, commonly with a minimum of USD 10,000, and should be wired into a dedicated Capital Escrow Account or the operational account using SWIFT MT103. For a USD transfer to Panama, the remitting bank sends the payment through a U.S. correspondent or directly by SWIFT MT103 to the receiving Panamanian bank's BIC, with the recipient's name and account number exactly matching the PIF's bank record. Field 70 should state: PIF CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / FOUNDATION CHARTER NO. [registration number]. Panama does not maintain an official FX purpose-code table; the remitter may map the transaction to the relevant SWIFT ISO purpose code, commonly GIFT for a funded endowment or INVE for a capital investment, while avoiding LOAN if the transaction is equity-like. Verification documents required by the receiving bank include the apostilled Foundation Charter, Registro Público good-standing certificate, Foundation Council resolution accepting the endowment and naming signatories, founder's passport, source-of-wealth documentation, and Travel Rule originator information showing the founder's name, address, and account number. Funds from a U.S. collection account can alternatively be sent by ACH to the SWIFT bridge and then as an MT103 cover payment to Panama.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For Amazon FBA outbound flows, the primary clearing rail is marketplace settlement: Amazon Seller Central pays net revenue via USD ACH or through a PSP to the PIF's U.S. collection account with Stripe, Airwallex, Payoneer, or Amazon Pay; the PIF then executes a treasury sweep by SWIFT MT103 into the Panamanian operational account. Direct Amazon payouts to a Panamanian local bank account are generally not available, so the U.S. or PSP collection account is the practical settlement hub. For supplier and inventory payments, open-account trade is cleared through SWIFT MT103 in USD, with CNY payments routed through Bank of China (Panama), S.A. via SWIFT or CIPS where required and fully documented with purchase orders and invoices. For higher-value or first-time suppliers, a commercial documentary letter of credit (UCP600) issued by a Panamanian bank and transmitted by SWIFT MT700 is permissible; the PIF typically collateralizes the L/C with USD term deposits at the issuing bank. Within Panama, low-value domestic transactions clear through the local ACH/clearinghouse operated under Banco Nacional de Panamá, while high-value USD positions settle through U.S. correspondent banks because Panama has no central-bank RTGS system; all outbound payments remain free of exchange control authorization.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH and CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDF) executed with a licensed Panamanian bank or an offshore regulated prime broker, backed by documented Amazon import/supplier exposure in China.
Deliverable USD/CNY or USD/HKD forwards arranged through Bank of China (Panama), S.A. or another SWIFT/CIPS-connected bank for physical CNY trade settlements.
USD/EUR and USD/GBP foreign-exchange forwards and FX swaps under ISDA 2002 or bilateral master FX agreements with SBP-licensed banks.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps between USD and operating foreign currencies for supplier credit, inventory financing, or long-term Amazon working-capital hedges.
European-style FX options and zero-cost collars purchased on a non-speculative cash-flow hedging basis for Amazon settlement proceeds and supplier disbursements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Private Interest Foundation annual government fee (Tasa Única Anual de Fundación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of USD 50 per month or fraction thereof; persistent non-payment may lead to cancellation of the foundation's registration and administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) — nil or substantive, depending on Panamanian-source activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March immediately following the fiscal tax year, unless otherwise stated in the RUC file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine from USD 50 to USD 5,000 dependent on delay and economic size; default surcharges, indexation, and possible criminal prosecution for willful failure to file after summons.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered agent annual compliance confirmation and beneficial-owner record update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained by the licensed registered agent; records producible to law enforcement and DGI upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before the foundation's registration anniversary, and within 30 days of any ownership or officer change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registered agent liability under Law 70 of 2019 and Money Laundering Regulations; civil fines and suspension of agent license for non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required when annual Panamanian-source gross income exceeds USD 3,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 5,000,000; otherwise no statutory audit for a PIF unless the foundation charter or a creditor requires one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted in Panama; a non-public PIF may apply IFRS for SMEs or the simplified accounting framework stated in the foundation charter.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama PIFs have no share capital and no public UBO registry filing. The licensed registered agent must maintain accurate beneficial-owner records, update them within 30 days of any change, and make them available to the competent authorities; unless the foundation is designated as an exempted or regulated entity, no annual public UBO declaration is submitted.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,000 per year if audited; no cost if below mandatory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panamanian-source income is subject to corporate income tax. Foreign-source e-commerce revenue (e.g., Amazon Marketplace sales directed to non-Panamanian customers) is generally exempt, yielding an effective 0% tax on such offshore income. No statutory tax holiday is available for this standard e-commerce activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 200 (Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) — filed electronically via the DGI ‘T@PA’ system at https://tapa.dgi.gob.pa/
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed on or before 31 March of the following year (within 3 months after fiscal year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income (Ingresos brutos) derived from Panamanian sources only. For an Amazon FBA business, include Panamanian sales; exclude foreign destination sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF has no Panamanian-sourced income, enter zero and attach a statement explaining territoriality.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and allowable costs (costos y gastos deducibles) directly attributable to Panama-source income, supported by invoices and contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses that satisfy the territorial nexus; foreign-related overheads are not deductible against Panama income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (renta neta gravable) after allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute strictly on Panama-source taxable revenue; losses from foreign e-commerce activities cannot reduce Panama taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax due at 25% over net taxable income, less any prepayments (anticipos) and foreign tax credits if a tax treaty applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs normally have no Panama prepayments; if zero taxable income, state zero due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accumulated losses carried forward from prior years (up to 5 years) and current-year adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Permitted only if the prior losses were recognized under Panama territorial rules; foreign losses are ineligible.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: from US$50 to US$10,000 depending on taxpayer history and revenue. A daily surcharge of 2% per month (max 30%) applies on unpaid income tax; failure to file may also trigger a 30% statutory penalty and administrative interest at 1.5% per month.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding rate under a Panama double tax treaty (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must (i) provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by their tax authority, (ii) complete Formulario 810 (Solicitud de Certificado de Residencia) at the Panama DGI, and (iii) submit the TRC and form to the withholding agent before the dividend distribution. Approval is required before applying the reduced rate; otherwise the 5% statutory rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 12.5% on payments to non-residents for use of intellectual property in Panama; treaty rates may reduce to 0%–10% if the DTA so provides. Interest: statutory 10% on interest derived from Panamanian financing (e.g., shareholder loans secured against Panama assets); treaty rates commonly reduce to 5% or 0% depending on the counterparty jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory when related-party transactions exceed B/. 1,000,000 (Panama Balboa, parity with USD) in a fiscal year; also required when gross income exceeds B/. 2,000,000. Transactions below these thresholds must nevertheless maintain contemporaneous evidence of arm's length pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regime (Ley 254 de 2018) applies to entities conducting 'relevant activities' such as distribution and service centers, headquarter operations, or IP holding. Cross-border e-commerce via Amazon FBA generally does not constitute a relevant activity unless the PIF engages in physical distribution or procurement functions within Panama. Taxpayers claiming treaty benefits must demonstrate economic substance (mind and management, employees, premises) to avoid being treated as a shell. The DGI may disregard the entity and reattribute income to the beneficial owner if substance is lacking.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Panama-source income, deliberately misstating deductions, or falsifying invoices to reduce taxable profit in the Formulario 200.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine equivalent to twice the evaded tax plus imprisonment from 2 to 6 years (Código Tributario). Civil penalty of 50% of the omitted tax and interest at 1.5% monthly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or foundation council members who knowingly sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes, civil penalties, and potential criminal prosecution (imprisonment up to 6 years); travel bans may be imposed during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with no employees, no office, no accounting records, and no beneficial owner identification while claiming tax treaty benefits or zero tax on international e-commerce income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Ley 254, the DGI may levy a fine of up to US$1,000,000 for failure to provide substance evidence; the entity may be disqualified as a 'resident' for tax purposes, causing full Panamanian-source and worldwide-source income to become taxable with retroactive interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or council members who knowingly assent to a sham foundation may be held personally accountable for the entity's tax liabilities and subjected to civil restitution orders, asset freezes, and criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: PIF fails to maintain beneficial ownership records, abandons KYC procedures for shareholders, or processes Amazon FBA proceeds through Panama accounts without transparent substance, thus masking the natural person behind the foundation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under the AML Law (Ley 23 de 2015) from US$10,000 to US$500,000 per violation; the PIF may be dissolved and its assets confiscated if used for money laundering; criminal penalties include imprisonment from 5 to 12 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, or foundation council members face criminal liability including up to 12 years' imprisonment, personal fines, asset forfeiture, and mandatory travel bans; professional licenses (legal, accounting) may be revoked.
